S04.meta: // SLIDE 04 — PHARMACOGENOMICS: Three gene-drug pairs where variant = standard dose becomes toxic overdose

tracks.label: Wild-type enzyme activity
tracks.outcome: Drug cleared at expected rate. Therapeutic exposure. Intended toxicity profile.

tracks.label: Loss-of-function variant
tracks.outcome: Drug accumulates to toxic concentrations. Functional overdose at standard dose. Fatalities documented.
notes: DPYD variant (3–5%): 5-FU → severe mucositis, neutropenia; EU mandates pre-treatment testing

S07.meta: // SLIDE 07 — WHY SINGLE TARGETS FAIL: P-gp inhibitors — lab success, clinical failure

data.question: Can blocking P-glycoprotein reverse MDR and improve outcomes?

branches.label: Laboratory model
branches.detail: P-gp inhibitor reverses efflux pump — drug accumulates in resistant cells, killing resumed. Elegant single-target logic.

branches.label: Clinical trial (1990s–2000s)
branches.detail: Normal gut and liver P-gp blockade alters pharmacokinetics — systemic toxicity increased. Parallel resistance routes (ABC transporters, enhanced repair, apoptosis evasion) left intact.
branches.fix: Failed — blocking one pump left five others running

resolver.label: Resistance is a system, not a leverage point
resolver.detail: Clinical tumor resistance is overlapping mechanisms. The productive frame: which combination drives this tumor, and does any create a new exploitable vulnerability?

S08.meta: // SLIDE 08 — MYELOSUPPRESSION: Nadir window timeline — the medical emergency defined by biology

modes.label: Post-dose (Day 1–6)
modes.sub: Mature circulating cells die without replacement. Counts falling.
modes.resolves: No clinical crisis yet — marrow depletion in progress

modes.label: Nadir window (Day 7–14)
modes.sub: ANC at lowest — febrile neutropenia threshold <500
modes.resolves: FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA = empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics NOW — do not wait for cultures. Sepsis risk from normal flora.

modes.label: Recovery (Day 21)
modes.sub: Counts recover toward baseline — 21-day cycle timed to this window
modes.resolves: Cycle 2 can proceed after count recovery confirmed

verdicts: febrile neutropenia is a medical emergency

S09.meta: // SLIDE 09 — NEUROPATHY & NAUSEA: Two toxicities, two opposite management logics

data.question: Can the toxicity be prevented or reversed?

branches.label: Peripheral neuropathy — platinum, taxanes, vinca, bortezomib
branches.detail: Cumulative — worsens with each cycle. Does not fully reverse when drug stopped. No established pharmacological prevention. Completing an effective regimen may produce permanent impairment.
branches.fix: Dose reduction or discontinuation — the only management

branches.label: Chemotherapy-induced nausea — cisplatin (highly emetogenic)
branches.detail: Modern prophylaxis: 5-HT3 antagonist + NK1 antagonist + olanzapine + dexamethasone. Transformed tolerability. Key: treat BEFORE cycle one — anticipatory nausea once conditioned is nearly untreatable.
branches.fix: Prevented with pre-treatment prophylaxis — biology-driven timing

resolver.label: Prophylaxis before cycle one is non-negotiable
resolver.detail: Anticipatory nausea is a conditioned response — prevent the first bad experience, or it cannot be undone. Each element of the supportive plan is a prediction acted on before the problem manifests.
